comparator.name: Archaeology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page accounts for the full 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year archaeology, 60 EC of compulsory second-year archaeology, and a third year with a 30-EC minor, 10 EC of archaeology theory and data/research design, a 10-EC IMPACT choice and a 10-EC bachelor thesis. It explicitly requires archaeological fieldwork in both first and second year, material conservation and archaeometry, GIS, geoarchaeology, archaeobotany, zooarchaeology and human osteoarchaeology. The programme page presents regional choices inside thematic modules rather than separate formal degree routes, so no route is selected. The 30-EC minor and the 10-EC IMPACT choice remain explicit rather than being populated with invented content.

exception.reason: The Groningen programme devotes 120 EC in its first two years to archaeology and then adds archaeological theory, data analysis, research design and a 10-EC archaeology thesis. Required study spans Greek and Roman, north-west European and Arctic archaeology; material culture, conservation and archaeometry; GIS and geoarchaeology; archaeobotany, zooarchaeology and human osteoarchaeology; and two credited fieldwork sequences. UCR has a small but valuable archaeology and heritage group—Introduction to World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology, and Heritage & Ancient Democracy—but no supervised excavation sequence, archaeological-materials or conservation laboratory sequence, bioarchaeology sequence, GIS/geoarchaeology sequence or archaeology thesis. Filling 24 places mainly with history, art, environmental science and generic methods would present neighbouring disciplines as an Archaeology bachelor. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can therefore be formed.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year archaeology, 60 EC of compulsory second-year archaeology, a 30-EC minor, 10 EC of archaeology theory/data/research-design study, a 10-EC IMPACT choice and a 10-EC archaeology thesis. The programme includes regional choices within thematic modules but no separate named degree route requiring selection. Genuine minor and IMPACT choice space is preserved without inventing content.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort availability. MCCHEAM112 introduces world archaeology through material culture; MCCHEAM213 studies Greek archaeology; and MCCHEAM315 links ancient democracy, material evidence and heritage. MCCHEAM211, MCCHEAM212, MCCHEAM111, MCCHEAM312 and MCCHEAM316 contribute art, museum and heritage study, but do not replace archaeological method. GOSHIST courses provide historical analysis; GOSHIST213 includes ancient warfare but is not excavation archaeology. Environmental and data courses may support landscape or digital questions, yet no UCR sequence teaches archaeological stratigraphy, supervised excavation, finds processing, artefact conservation, archaeometry, GIS for archaeology, archaeobotany, zooarchaeology, osteoarchaeology or an independent archaeology thesis. A 24-course archaeology-led programme cannot pass the specific course-to-concept and coherence gates.
